1	# Production deployment
2	
3	How to stand DataQ up in production. This is the operator's overview; the exhaustive
4	provisioning runbook, the OpenTofu stack, and the complete env-var reference live in
5	[`deploy/README.md`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/README.md) and
6	[`deploy/terraform/azure/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/azure).
7	Azure is the supported target today; AWS/GCP are planned behind the same seams.
8	
9	## Topology
10	
11	```
12	Browser ──HTTPS──► Frontend Container App (nginx + SPA — the ONLY public ingress)
13	AI clients ─MCP──► │  proxies /api + /mcp + /healthz same-origin
14	                   ▼
15	              FastAPI (internal ingress) ──► PostgreSQL
16	                   │  ├──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► your datasources
17	                   │  ├──► Redis (task queue)
18	                   │  ├──► Key Vault (secrets)
19	                   │  └──► App Insights / OTLP (observability)
20	```
21	
22	The frontend is the sole public surface; the API is internal and reached only through the
23	frontend proxy (ADR 0028 §5).
24	
25	## Prerequisites
26	
27	- A **container platform** — Azure Container Apps in the reference deploy (API + worker +
28	  frontend apps, a one-shot migrate **job**, and Redis).
29	- **PostgreSQL** (a dedicated database + a least-privilege app role).
30	- A **secret store** — Azure Key Vault, reached via a managed identity.
31	- An **OIDC identity provider** — app registrations for the API (audience) and the SPA.
32	- **Observability** — Application Insights and/or a generic OTLP endpoint.
33	- A container registry the platform can pull from (GHCR in the reference).
34	
35	## 1. Provision
36	
37	Use the in-repo OpenTofu stack ([`deploy/terraform/azure/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/azure),
38	ADR 0024) to stand up the app stack — the Container Apps, the migrate job, Redis, Key Vault +
39	managed identity, App Insights, and the SSO app registrations — plus a dedicated database and
40	least-priv role on your Postgres server. Set the required **GitHub environment variables and
41	Key Vault secrets** (full list in the deploy README) — never ship the eval/dev defaults.
42	
43	## 2. Deploy
44	
45	Deployment is a **manual GitHub Actions workflow** (`workflow_dispatch` → **Deploy**). Each
46	run, in order:
47	
48	1. **Builds + pushes** the backend and frontend images (tag defaults to the immutable commit
49	   SHA).
50	2. **Runs migrations** — a Container Apps job runs `alembic upgrade head` and the workflow
51	   **waits for it to succeed** *before* rolling anything. Migrations are additive/
52	   backward-compatible, so the still-running old code tolerates the new schema.
53	3. **Rolls** the API + worker, then the frontend (gated on the backend succeeding — no partial
54	   deploys).
55	
56	Use an immutable image tag per release; push-on-merge is intentionally off.
57	
58	## 3. Verify
59	
60	Run the **pre-deploy** and **post-deploy smoke** checklists in
61	[`deploy/README.md`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/README.md#pre-deploy-checklist)
62	around every deploy. In short:
63	
64	- **Before:** CI green on the SHA, docs up to date, migrations safe, secrets/config in place.
65	- **After:** `/healthz` → 200; a user can **sign in**; the **UI renders** (key pages, desktop
66	  + mobile); **every high-level flow works** end-to-end; auth is enforced (`401` on the API
67	  and MCP — MCP must be `401`, **not** `421`); prod docs are gated (`404`); and the api /
68	  worker / frontend are on the deployed tag with the migrate job `Succeeded`.
69	
70	## Running DataQ without Azure
71	
72	Azure is **one implementation behind each seam, never the architecture** (ADR
73	[0010](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md)).
74	Every seam has a working non-Azure implementation, so a fresh clone runs the
75	whole product — API, worker, scheduler, UI, checks — with **zero Azure
76	configuration** (#591):
77	
78	| Seam | Azure implementation | Local / non-Azure implementation |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| Secrets | Key Vault (`SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`) | `SECRET_STORE=openbao` — OpenBao in compose (the default in `.env.app.example`), or `env` for host-only dev. ADR [0039](adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md); the store speaks the KV v2 API, so the same mode also serves Vault or HCP |
81	| Auth | Entra SSO (`AZURE_*`) | **Email OTP** for humans (`AUTH_EMAIL_*` + an allowlist — ADR [0032](adr/0032-email-otp-signin.md)); `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true` for local dev; **PATs** (`dq_live_…`) for headless REST/MCP — see [API keys](api-keys.md). `/mcp` is served in every one of these modes; under OTP it accepts **PATs only** (no IdP ⇒ no bearer token to validate) |
82	| Observability | App Insights connection string | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` → any OTLP consumer; `docker-compose --profile telemetry up` starts a local Jaeger (UI on `:16686`). Unset ⇒ telemetry off, which is a supported posture, not a degraded one |
83	| Queue / cache | — | Redis in compose (same image as prod) |
84	| Database | Shared Azure Postgres | Postgres in compose |
85	| Lineage catalog | — | `docker-compose --profile lineage up` starts Marquez (dev-only reference consumer, ADR 0034) |
86	
87	```bash
88	git clone <repo> && cd DataQ
89	./scripts/setup.sh          # conda env, hooks, images, migrations, seed data
90	docker-compose up           # postgres + redis + openbao + api + worker + frontend
91	```
92	
93	`.env.app.example` ships with the local-first values already selected
94	(`SECRET_STORE=openbao`, `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, both telemetry endpoints blank);
95	every `AZURE_*` key may stay empty. Nothing in the app reads an Azure SDK unless
96	the corresponding seam is explicitly pointed at Azure.
97	
98	**What is not available locally** is *datasources*, not the platform: a
99	Snowflake or ADLS **connection** needs a live Snowflake or ADLS to run against.
100	The local-first path keeps flat files (local + S3), Unity Catalog (Databricks
101	Free Edition), and Iceberg. The test suite is unaffected either way — its
102	datasource reads are stubbed, so `pytest` is green with no cloud credentials of
103	any kind.
104	
105	## Operating notes
106	
107	- **Backward-compatible migrations only** — no `DROP`/rename/`NOT NULL`-without-default in the
108	  same release as the code that needs it. An `ALTER` on a hot table can briefly block on a
109	  live-worker lock; recovery + hardening are documented in the deploy README.
110	- **Secrets rotate** without a redeploy (they're read from the store at runtime); restart the
111	  dependent apps after a shared-Postgres recreate (start-time secret snapshot).
112	- The reference deployment carries **demo/test fixtures** — tear them down before any
113	  customer-facing or marketplace use (see the deploy README's operational notes).
114

116	the checklists — see

## AWS reference deployment

The same product deploys to AWS from the in-repo OpenTofu stack
([`deploy/terraform/aws/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/aws)) —
identical images, identical topology, each seam pointed at the AWS implementation:

```
Browser ──HTTPS──► CloudFront (public surface, origin secret verified at nginx)
                   ▼
              ALB ──► frontend (ECS Fargate, nginx + SPA) ──proxies──► api (ECS Fargate)
                   │  api/worker sidecars: ADOT collector → X-Ray traces + CloudWatch logs
                   ├──► RDS PostgreSQL          ├──► ElastiCache Redis (TLS)
                   ├──► AWS Secrets Manager     └──► SES (email alerts)
              Cognito (OIDC issuer for the SPA + API)
```

- **Secrets:** `SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager` (fourth store behind the seam).
- **Auth:** Amazon Cognito through the same generic OIDC contract (`DATAQ_AUTH_*`,
  `AUTH_OIDC_*`) — the second issuer validated in a real deployment after Azure AD. Cognito
  needs `DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE=cognito` (its `/logout` is not RP-Initiated-Logout
  conformant) and resolves the user profile via the **userinfo endpoint** (its access tokens
  carry neither `email` nor `aud`).
- **Observability:** the app's vendor-neutral OTLP export feeds an **ADOT collector sidecar**
  → X-Ray traces + OpenTelemetry logs in CloudWatch with matching trace ids.
- **Deploy:** a parallel **Deploy (AWS)** workflow (`deploy-aws.yml`) — GitHub OIDC role
  login, immutable `aws-<sha>` tags, migrate run-task gated on exit 0, then ECS service
  rolls and a CloudFront smoke.
- **Gotchas** (full list in the
  [AWS README](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/terraform/aws/README.md)):
  a `rediss://` broker URL needs `ssl_cert_reqs` (the app now defaults it to `required`);
  task definitions are under `ignore_changes`, so env/sidecar edits need a targeted
  `tofu apply -replace`; CloudFront sends an **origin secret header** that nginx enforces,
  so a third-party distribution cannot origin-point at the ALB.
